title: t4: pointer-then-lookup in a 2-layer benchmark transformer (mlp0 -> head 1.1 -> mlp1)
behavior: Input BOS + 6 tokens from {fu=2, ko=3, ni=4, pa=5, tu=6}; the model outputs one symbol at the last position.
label: verified
summary: The output depends on only two input tokens: the last token t6 and one token x from positions 1-3, chosen by t6 (ko -> position 1, ni -> position 3, fu/pa/tu -> position 2). The output is a fixed 5x5 lookup TABLE[t6][x]. Positions 4 and 5 are never used. Circuit: mlp0 supplies the pointer derived from the last token, head 1.1 attends one-hot from the last position to the pointed position, mlp1 produces the output. Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0, 1.2 play no part. All numbers are from local-full (full precision). Held-out verification V0002 (n=400, unused seed): predict() agrees with the model on 100% of inputs; ablating the circuit drops the metric to 0.002 of clean (accuracy 0.21, chance 0.2); ablating everything else leaves 1.0.
pseudocode:
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    last = tokens[6]                      # fu=2 ko=3 ni=4 pa=5 tu=6
    ptr = {3: 1, 4: 3}.get(last, 2)       # mlp0 + head 1.1: ko->pos1, ni->pos3, fu/pa/tu->pos2
    x = tokens[ptr]                       # head 1.1 copies the pointed token
    TABLE = {                             # mlp1
        2: {2: 3, 3: 3, 4: 3, 5: 4, 6: 6},
        3: {2: 3, 3: 4, 4: 4, 5: 2, 6: 5},
        4: {2: 5, 3: 2, 4: 4, 5: 3, 6: 6},
        5: {2: 5, 3: 5, 4: 2, 5: 2, 6: 2},
        6: {2: 2, 3: 6, 4: 3, 5: 4, 6: 3},
    }
    return TABLE[last][x]

claims.text: The model performs a deterministic behaviour: accuracy 1.0 against its own outputs on 64 inputs.

The function is output = TABLE[t6][x], x = token at position 1 (t6=ko), 3 (t6=ni) or 2 (t6=fu/pa/tu). On 400 held-out inputs this code matches the model 100% (task-shuffled null: mean 0.22, max 0.27). A first version with one mis-transcribed table entry ([pa][tu]) matched 98%, with all 4 misses on exactly that entry.

Head 1.1 implements the pointer: from the last position its attention is 1.0 on position 1 for ko-ending inputs, 1.0 on position 3 for ni-ending inputs and 1.0 on position 2 for fu/pa/tu-ending inputs.
Head 1.1 and mlp1 are necessary: joint mean ablation leaves 0.015 of the clean metric.

mlp0 is part of the circuit and its role is consistent with supplying the pointer: mean-ablating it is harmless when all inputs share the same pointer (fu/pa/tu-ending, 1.0 of clean) and destructive when the pointers differ (ko/ni-ending, 0.30 of clean). The original prediction that everything outside {1.1, mlp1} is inert was refuted (0.66 of clean, predicted >= 0.9).
Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0 and 1.2 play no part: jointly mean-ablating them leaves 1.0 of the clean metric, and with everything outside {mlp0, 1.1, mlp1} ablated the model keeps accuracy 1.0.

The circuit {mlp0, 1.1, mlp1} is necessary and sufficient on held-out data: circuit ablated -> 0.002 of clean (accuracy 0.2125); everything else ablated -> 1.0 of clean (accuracy 1.0); both beyond every null control.

nodes.label: head 1.1: one-hot attention to pointed position, copies x

limitations: The mlp0 -> head 1.1 query edge was not measured directly: path_patching with sender mlp0 raised a ValueError, so the pointer role of mlp0 rests on conditional mean ablations (E0013, E0014) plus the attention patterns. Those do not exclude that mlp0 writes the pointer at a position other than the last one, nor a role beyond the pointer that happens to be shared by fu/pa/tu.
How mlp1 receives t6 (directly from the embedding via the residual stream) was not isolated.
The lookup table was read off input/output pairs (E0001) and confirmed behaviourally; no structure inside mlp1 was analysed. The table looks arbitrary and I found no simpler closed form.
Attribution patching (E0002) assigned mlp0 zero effect; that first-order estimate was wrong, as the ablations showed.
E0010-E0012 (per-component sweeps, mlp_out patching) were exploratory and are used only as pointers to the pre-registered runs.
open_questions: Does mlp0 encode the pointer as a position index read by 1.1's query at the last position only?
Is there any simpler rule that generates the 5x5 table?

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: Everything except head 1.1 and mlp1 is inert: jointly mean-ablating heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0, 1.2 and mlp0 leaves the behaviour intact.

prediction.statement: Joint mean ablation of all non-circuit components keeps at least 90% of the clean metric
